item.title: The louder protectionism roars, the more precious China-EU dialogue becomes: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 00:52:00
China EU Photo:VCG At a time when global challenges continue to emerge, the significance of China-EU relations has long extended beyond the bilateral sphere. By continuously deepening their economic ties and shared interests, China and the EU can not only unleash the innovative potential of their respective markets but also reinforce each other's development and contribute to global economic recovery. From Thursday to Friday, China and the EU held the second meeting of their bilateral trade and investment consultation mechanism in Beijing. The two sides engaged in pragmatic and productive discussions, reaching a 16-point consensus covering trade and investment balances, export controls, intellectual property rights and reform of the World Trade Organization (WTO). Against the backdrop of a sluggish global economic recovery and undercurrents of anti-globalization, this is a pragmatic step to properly handle bilateral differences and a crucial display of responsibility by China and the EU in injecting stability and certainty into the global economy amid turbulent times. A closer look at this list reveals its core value: anchored in rules-based governance and bridged by mutual trust, it demonstrates the political wisdom to manage differences and steer China-EU economic and trade relations toward greater stability and balance. The first item on the list states that both sides will continue to explore the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain products within the WTO framework. In the hybrid vehicle trade sector, which has attracted significant public attention, the two sides agreed to reach a mutual understanding in a manner consistent with WTO rules, providing a pathway to ease the previously deadlocked trade dispute. In the field of export controls, China expressed its willingness to continue facilitating export license approvals for rare earths and permanent magnets bound for the EU through a "green channel" mechanism. The two sides also included "advance notifications before items are added to control lists" in the consensus list. This arrangement improves the transparency in listing and delisting procedures, helping to reduce misjudgments and stabilize expectations. This list covers a significant portion of the current challenges and bottlenecks in economic and trade relations between China and the EU, and the consensus reached by both sides demonstrates that no matter how complex trade frictions may be, pragmatic solutions can always be found as long as both sides uphold the spirit of dialogue and adhere to equal-footed consultation. The convergence of interests is the inevitable outcome of economic globalization and more so a powerful engine driving common prosperity for China, the EU, and the world at large. In 2025, China-EU trade in goods exceeded $800 billion, with their combined economic output accounting for over one-third of the global total, bilateral trade volume making up nearly one-quarter of the world's total, and nearly half of bilateral trade consisting of intermediate goods. The long-standing pattern of "trade surpluses in China and profits in Europe" has made the two sides a community of shared interests, with each deeply intertwined with the other. This also demonstrates that as long as China and the EU work together, the synergies they generate will far outweigh the narrow calculations of a zero-sum game, creating vast new opportunities for industrial upgrading and improving the well-being of their peoples. Protectionism cannot enhance competitiveness, while decoupling and severing supply chains will only harm others without benefiting oneself. By continuously deepening their economic ties and shared interests, China and the EU can not only unleash the innovative potential of their respective markets but also reinforce each other's development and contribute to global economic recovery. As a major strategic force in the world, Europe should uphold its tradition of multilateralism and strategic autonomy, rather than allow itself to be swept up in the tide of protectionism and the excessive securitization of economic issues. At the moment, unilateralism is on the rise, with certain major powers frequently imposing sanctions in an attempt to weaponize economic and trade issues. Europe has a deep-rooted tradition of free trade and should not simply follow the crowd, much less turn security anxieties into trade barriers. As China has repeatedly and sincerely pointed out, the EU should remain committed to openness, cooperation and free trade, abide by WTO rules, not resort to protectionist tools at every turn, and, above all, refrain from politicizing and excessively securitizing economic and trade issues - so as to avoid pursuing misguided policies that will ultimately backfire on itself. China is not the root cause of the EU's problems, but a partner in addressing them. Faced with a complex external environment, Europe can only truly safeguard its fundamental interests amid changes unseen in a century by taking a long-term view of the economic and trade relations between China and the EU and adhering to equal-footed dialogue and consultation. Looking ahead to future arrangements for institutionalized consultations, China and the EU should overcome obstacles through sustained dialogue and work together to provide stability and certainty to the world. The two sides have agreed to hold the third regular meeting under the mechanism in March 2027 and maintain close communication in the meantime, including a ministerial-level video meeting in January 2027. Such institutionalized and regular arrangements provide an important safeguard for bridging differences and deepening cooperation. At a time when global challenges continue to emerge, the significance of China-EU relations has long extended beyond the bilateral sphere. In the face of an international landscape marked by intertwined turbulence and transformation, China and the EU should be partners that build mutual trust rather than systemic rivals, and promoters of cooperation rather than instigators of friction. We look forward to both China and the EU seizing this opportunity presented by the consultations to continue deepening cooperation based on equal dialogue and mutual benefit, translating more consensus into concrete actions, ensuring that the benefits of China-EU economic and trade cooperation continue to benefit the people of both sides, and injecting more warmth and confidence into a global economy fraught with uncertainty.

item.title: Chinese national killed in attack on construction site in Nigeria's Kebbi State: report
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 00:33:00
Map of Kebbi State in Nigeria Photo: screenshot from a Channels Television report A Chinese national was killed along with two local security personnel in an attack on a construction site in Nigeria's Kebbi State on Thursday, the Xinhua News Agency reported on Friday, citing local police. According to Xinhua, the Kebbi State Police Command said in a statement on Friday that armed men entered the area from neighboring Sokoto State and attacked a construction site, killing a foreign national and two local security personnel. Police confirmed to Xinhua on Friday that the foreign national killed in the attack was a Chinese citizen, according to the report. Two other people were injured in the attack and taken to hospital for treatment, according to the police statement. Police also said they repelled another attack elsewhere in Kebbi State on Thursday, and security forces have been deployed to the affected areas to strengthen security, Xinhua reported. Global Times

item.title: China, EU reach consensus on areas including hybrid vehicles, rare earths after Beijing talks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 00:13:00
China EU Photo:VCG China and the European Union (EU) reached a 16-point consensus spanning trade and investment, export controls, intellectual property rights and World Trade Organization (WTO) reform at high-level talks in Beijing on Thursday and Friday, marking tangible progress in efforts to manage bilateral differences even as protectionist pressure continued to build within Europe. The outcomes included an understanding on hybrid vehicle trade, measures to facilitate rare-earth export licensing and further discussions on market access and trade barriers, according to a joint statement released by China's Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) on Friday. Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic held the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation (TIC) mechanism on October 8-9, engaging in pragmatic and productive discussions, according to the joint statement. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment as key trading partners to properly managing differences under WTO rules, maintaining stable bilateral economic and trade ties and making them more balanced. They agreed to hold the third meeting in March 2027 and maintain close communication in the meantime, including a ministerial-level video meeting in January. The exchanges have drawn widespread attention, coming at a critical juncture for China-EU economic ties and just days before an October 15 to 16 EU summit in Brussels, where the bloc's trade relations with China are expected to feature prominently. Chinese analysts said the agreement underscored the value of institutionalized dialogue in managing disputes, while offering a path toward common solutions and bringing greater predictability for future economic ties. They also urged the EU to follow through on the consensus in good faith and avoid allowing protectionist pressures to undermine the progress made through dialogue. From dialogue to progress Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng met with Sefcovic in Beijing on Friday, calling on both sides to make full use of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, maintain a stable and balanced partnership as key trading partners, and properly manage differences through continued dialogue. Sefcovic said China was an important economic and trade partner of the EU, expressing willingness to advance trade and investment consultations and strengthen cooperation. Among the key outcomes, China and the EU agreed to continue exploring the possibility of lowering tariffs on certain products under WTO rules. The two sides also reached an understanding on hybrid vehicle trade in line with WTO rules. On electric vehicles (EVs), they agreed to continue procedures related to company-specific price undertakings and reviews under the EU's anti-subsidy investigation into Chinese EVs. On export controls, China expressed its willingness to continue facilitating export license approvals for rare earths and permanent magnets bound for the EU through a "green channel." The EU, in turn, will continue working with member states to facilitate the resolution of priority cases involving export licenses for dual-use items destined for China. The high-level talks under the trade and investment consultation framework provided an important platform for managing differences over trade, industrial cooperation and supply chains, Cui Hongjian, a professor at the Academy of Regional and Global Governance at Beijing Foreign Studies University, told the Global Times on Friday. Cui said the talks showed that both sides were willing to address trade disputes through dialogue. "Beyond the specific agreements, the talks could help establish a more predictable framework for managing differences and bring greater stability to China-EU economic relations," he added. Shi Kang, a chair professor at Tsinghua University's PBC School of Finance, told the Global Times that the talks marked a key test of whether months of intensive negotiations could deliver tangible progress on issues ranging from new-energy industries to trade barriers and industrial rules. The China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism was established on June 29, when Wang and Šefčovič chaired its inaugural meeting in Brussels and set up four working groups on trade and investment balancing, export controls, intellectual property rights and WTO reform. By late July, the two sides had each held more than 20 consultations, according to MOFCOM. While China and the EU broadly share the goal of resolving trade disputes, Cui noted that they still differ over the pace and approach to resolving them. "China favors a reasonable, orderly process, while the EU tends to link negotiations to its domestic political agenda and timetable," he said. Cui stressed the need for both sides to align their expectations and build on the progress made through continued consultations. China has always believed that it serves the shared interests of China and the EU to stay committed to openness and cooperation, and resolve economic and trade disputes through equal-footed dialogue and consultation, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday. A call for pragmatism During the talks in Beijing, Wang Wentao expressed concern over the EU's recent trade and economic restrictions, reiterating that China is not the source of the EU's problems, but a partner in solving them. He urged the EU to properly manage trade frictions and differences through dialogue and consultation, in accordance with WTO rules and with due consideration for each other's interests, according to the MOFCOM. Wang's concerns come amid mounting calls for tougher trade measures against China from European industry groups and political circles. In the latest move, 44 European industry associations representing sectors including metals, chemicals and automotive parts urged EU member states to act against what they called unfair Chinese trade practices that threatened European manufacturing and jobs, Reuters reported on Thursday. The groups also urged the EU to make more effective use of existing trade defense measures, take a broader approach covering entire value chains, the report said. Just a day before the Beijing talks, the European Parliament also called for tougher action against China's alleged "economic coercion" and urged the EU to consider using its Anti-Coercion Instrument over critical raw materials concerns in a report on EU-China relations. Responding on Friday, a spokesperson for the Chinese Mission to the EU expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to the report, saying it was steeped in ideological bias, advocates for the politicization of economic and trade issues and the overstretching of the concept of security in such matters. The EU needs to recognize that its current difficulties stem not from China, but from its own structural decline, marked by sluggish innovation, slow industrial transformation, a failure to develop new growth drivers and eroding competitiveness, Wang Yiwei, director of the Institute of International Affairs and the Center for European Studies at Renmin University of China, told the Global Times on Friday. Resorting to short-term trade restrictions to address long-term industrial woes is a misguided approach, Wang said. "What Europe needs is industrial renewal, technological breakthroughs, digital transformation and stronger homegrown competitiveness - not blaming China or fueling trade confrontation." According to the MOFCOM, both sides viewed the second meeting as a new starting point for deeper China-EU cooperation and tasked their working teams with advancing follow-up work, ensuring the agreed outcomes are implemented as soon as possible and preparing for the third meeting of the trade and investment consultation mechanism. Wang Yiwei added that despite their differences, deep economic ties and industrial complementarities made comprehensive China-EU decoupling unrealistic. "Continued dialogue and cooperation between the two sides would be important not only for bilateral relations but also for the broader multilateral trading system," he said.

item.title: Beijing condemns Tokyo's use of AI to whitewash war crimes
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 00:08:00
Chinese Foreign Ministry China's Foreign Ministry on Friday slammed Japanese right-wing forces for using artificial intelligence (AI) to distort historical facts and whitewash Japan's crimes of aggression, calling on the international community to stay alert and reject such moves. The response came amid reports that Japan's right-wing forces are making continuous efforts to tamper World War II (WWII) history by entering adulterated data into mainstream AI models, some of which produce outputs with a clearly misguided view of history. For instance, they refer to the July 7 Incident as a "clash" between Japanese and Chinese troops, the Nanjing Massacre as the "Fall of Nanjing" and Japan's aggression against Southeast Asia as "interest" in the region's resources. Chinese experts warned that whitewashing wartime crimes serves Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's push to loosen postwar military restraints, urging countries that suffered Japanese aggression to remain vigilant. AI data poisoning Japan committed ironclad and undeniable crimes during its militarist aggression. Using new technologies to poison the data is the latest method by Japanese right-wing forces to distort and glorify Japan's war history, spokesperson Mao Ning said at Friday's regular press conference. The aim is to embed a wrong perception of WWII history and misguide public opinion, so that Japan can break free from its postwar pacifist constraint and accelerate remilitarization, she said. "AI should be used for the positive and for good, not for tampering with historical facts and whitewashing war crimes," Mao added. The covert moves of Japanese right-wing forces greatly hurt the sentiments of Japan's war victims and constitute a blatant affront to human conscience. The international community must stay on high alert and push back against those moves, Mao said. Science and Technology Daily, a Chinese media outlet that focuses on technology, warned on September 18 that Gennai, the Japanese government's AI platform, could become an official channel for spreading selective historical narratives. The newspaper said its source material favored current government positions while excluding prewar archives, including the Japanese Instrument of Surrender and Tokyo Trials records, creating a risk of distorted answers on history, territorial disputes and war responsibility. Japan's Digital Agency says the Gennai pilot targets about 180,000 government employees, with full-scale use planned for fiscal 2027. Citing Japan News, the English-language website of Yomiuri Shimbun, Science and Technology Daily reported plans to promote Gennai in Southeast Asia and elsewhere. It warned that exporting biased systems could spread distorted views of World War II and contaminate the wider information environment. Japanese right-wing forces have long sought to erase Japan's aggression through language, including the use of the wartime label "Greater East Asia War", Zhou Yongsheng, a professor at China Foreign Affairs University, told the Global Times on Friday. Japan has long portrayed its war of aggression against China and other Asian countries during World War II as "liberating Asians from Western colonial rule" while imposing fresh aggression, exploitation and colonial rule, Zhou said. AI is now being exploited as another channel for such narratives, including relabeling the Nanjing Massacre as the "Fall of Nanjing" and describing aggression in Southeast Asia as "interest" in regional resources, he said. Japan's right-wing forces have not only used AI to whitewash the country's wartime atrocities and attempt to reshape its history of aggression, but also used the technology to shape anti-China opinion. In December 2025, Asahi Shimbun reported that at least seven postings on crowdsourcing platform CrowdWorks before December 3 had sought scripts or AI-assisted editing for YouTube videos criticizing China and praising Japan. Two requests explicitly sought fictional episodes portraying Chinese people negatively. Some required applicants to love Japan and hate China. One reference video used machine-generated narration to recount an alleged American couple's experience, contrasting supposedly dirty Chinese cities and trains with clean Japanese ones, the newspaper reported. Alert on neo-militarism drive At the UN on Thursday, Chinese envoy Sun Xiaobo warned that Japan's accelerating remilitarization threatened regional peace and stability, according to CCTV News. Sun, director-general of the Foreign Ministry's Department of Arms Control, headed China's delegation to the First Committee of the 81st UN General Assembly. Sun noted that 2026 marks the UN's 81st anniversary and the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. Japan had joined the UN on the condition that it acknowledged its militarist crimes and accepted the UN Charter in full, he said. Sun said the postwar order faced serious challenges and accused Japan's current administration of denying aggression, glorifying war crimes and honoring WWII war criminals while expanding its military. He urged Japan to break with militarism, abandon remilitarization and fulfill its nuclear non-proliferation obligations. Sun's remarks followed comments by Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi on a BS Fuji program on September 28. Discussing the possession of nuclear weapons and nuclear-powered submarines, Koizumi called for debate "without taboos or predetermined conclusions", Kyodo News reported. Sun also criticized Japan's proposal to remove the "enemy state" clauses from the UN Charter, calling it the latest example of Tokyo challenging the postwar international order under the guise of becoming a "normal country." Lü Chao, an expert at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times that the Takaichi administration is brazen in terms of defending and excusing wartime crimes. Its support from right-wing forces, alongside expanded arms exports, weapons production and long-range missile deployments, reflected a neo-militarism trend threatening the region, he told the Global Times on Friday. Takaichi was using hardline sentiment to build support for constitutional revision, looser arms-export rules and military expansion. Whitewashing aggression and portraying Japan as a victim of Chinese pressure helped persuade the public to support the government in abandoning its exclusively defense-oriented policy, he said. The international community should guard against Japan's militarist ambitions concealed behind claims of being a peaceful country, Lü warned.

item.title: China rolls out 19 measures for new quality productive forces
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09 23:18:00
Robots stage a performance at the 22nd China (Shenzhen) International Cultural Industries Fair in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, May 24, 2026. Photo: Xinhua The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the State Council have issued guidelines to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces, setting out 19 key measures to strengthen technological innovation, deepen its integration with industry and improve institutional support for high-quality development. The document was made public on Friday. The guidelines cover five main areas, including technological and industrial innovation, innovation in development approaches, institutional reform and talent management. They identify developing new quality productive forces as an inherent requirement and a key priority for promoting high-quality development, with a substantial increase in total factor productivity as the core indicator. The document provides detailed arrangements for the systematic undertaking of developing new quality productive forces, Tian Yun, a Beijing-based economist, told the Global Times on Friday, while highlighting stronger support for enterprises' role in technological innovation as an important institutional innovation underpinning this effort. The guidelines call for establishing a corporate research and development reserve system, increasing the additional tax deduction rate for R&D expenses of technology-oriented small and medium-sized enterprises, and supporting capable private enterprises in leading major national technological research tasks. Enterprise R&D projects that meet national strategic needs can be elevated to national projects through prescribed procedures. Tian said coordination between the government and the market could help identify innovative projects across regions and industry segments, supporting the development of emerging industries. To accelerate commercialization, the document proposes deploying research and commercialization tasks together when technological projects are initiated and assessing actual application results upon completion. It also encourages universities and research institutions to license technological achievements to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises on a use-first, pay-later basis. The new guidelines combine traditional industrial upgrading with emerging and future industry development, placing particular emphasis on fully implementing the "AI Plus" initiative. They call for sector-specific AI pilot application bases and high-value application scenarios to accelerate adoption across industries. "Developing new quality productive forces is not about simply abandoning traditional industries, but rather empowering the existing real economy with intelligent technologies, so that old industries can regain new vitality," Xi Junyang, a professor at the Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, told the Global Times on Friday. AI can be widely applied across industries, making it an important avenue for developing new quality productive forces, Xi Junyang said, adding that it can advance technology while accelerating the large-scale application of technologies in traditional industries. China's high-tech manufacturing sector has maintained strong growth. Its value-added output among large enterprises rose 16.7 percent year-on-year in August, compared with 5.2 percent growth in overall industrial output. Industrial robot production increased 34.6 percent, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. The guidelines also call for advancing the energy revolution, developing advanced nuclear fission energy in an orderly manner, building a power system with a high proportion of renewable energy, and improving renewable energy integration and regulation policies. Xi Junyang said the energy revolution provides a reliable and secure foundation for developing new quality productive forces. It is an important arena for technological and industrial transformation, a path toward carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, and a source of security support for new growth drivers, he added. Alongside innovation support, the document sets requirements for orderly development. It calls for cross-regional industrial cooperation to avoid "involution-style" competition and mechanisms to increase investment and share risks in future industries. It also seeks stronger patient capital support for early-stage, small and hard-technology businesses. Localities must tailor their approaches to actual conditions, the guidelines state, warning against speculative expansion, industrial hollowing-out and blindly pursuing new industries. They prohibit the improper use of policies in the name of developing new quality productive forces and require serious accountability in cases where investment stampedes or blind investment cause major losses. The document also encourages foreign venture capital institutions to develop in China and calls for global innovation cooperation networks. Tian said the package could inject fresh momentum into Chinese modernization while generating positive spillover effects, enabling international partners to share opportunities arising from China's technological advances and development.

item.title: Botswana's president to pay state visit to China; China-Botswana cooperation offer lessons for African nations to advance economic transition: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09 23:10:00
File photo: VCG President of the Republic of Botswana Duma Gideon Boko will pay a state visit to China from October 12 to 17, the Chinese Foreign Ministry announced on Friday, and spokesperson Mao Ning said the upcoming visit will elevate China-Botswana relations to a new height and further contribute to building an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future for the new era. When elaborating on details of the visit at the regular press conference, Mao said this will be President Boko's first visit to China since he assumed office. The two heads of state will hold talks. Besides, President Boko will pay a visit to East China's Fujian Province. By noting that China and Botswana are strategic partners, the spokesperson said that over the 51 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the two countries have upheld sincere friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation. The two countries support each other on major issues concerning respective core interests, assist each other in times of disaster and epidemic, join hands on the journey toward modernization, and firmly stand on the right side of history on international affairs, said Mao. China and Botswana elevated their bilateral ties to a strategic partnership in September 2024. In January 2025, the two heads of state exchanged congratulatory messages marking the 50th anniversary of the establishment of China-Botswana diplomatic relations. According to Song Wei, a professor at the School of International Relations and Diplomacy at Beijing Foreign Studies University, the upcoming visit marks an important strategic alignment between the two countries. It builds on more than half a century of friendly relations and provides a key opportunity to deepen the strategic partnership through practical implementation. "The visit is expected to further consolidate bilateral strategic mutual trust and enable closer communication on issues concerning each side's core interests and major concerns," Song said. "It is also expected that the visit will advance practical cooperation by translating policy alignment into concrete projects and deeper cooperation." According to data from the Chinese Foreign Ministry, bilateral trade between China and Botswana reached $1.222 billion in 2025, representing a year-on-year increase of 21.3 percent. China's exports amounted to $300 million, growing 24.9 percent year-on-year, while imports stood at $922 million, an increase of 20.2 percent year-on-year. China mainly exports machinery and equipment, transport vehicles, and light industrial and textile products, and primarily imports diamonds and copper concentrates. According to experts, the strong complementarity in resource endowments and industrial capabilities between China and Botswana has laid a solid foundation for deeper cooperation. "Botswana is a major diamond producer in Africa, with rich reserves of copper, nickel and other minerals, while China possesses a full industrial chain spanning mineral extraction, smelting, processing and equipment manufacturing," said Song. Botswana also has abundant solar resources, while China enjoys strong industrial advantages in photovoltaic power generation, energy storage equipment, water-saving agriculture and digital agriculture, said the expert. She added that as a landlocked country, Botswana's development is constrained by transport, logistics and limited market size. China has rich experience in industrial park development, industrial chain cultivation, transportation, logistics and infrastructure construction. 2026 is designated as the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges and constitutes a pivotal year for delivering outcomes of the 2024 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit. Since May 1, China has implemented zero-tariff treatment for all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations. It continues negotiations with African nations on the Framework Agreement on Economic Partnership for Shared Development, to which Botswana is a signatory. Deeper bilateral cooperation will not only help Botswana pursue an industrialization and modernization path suited to its national conditions, but also serve as a model for China-Africa cooperation, Song said. According to the expert, many African countries rely heavily on resource exports and have underdeveloped industrial chains. Deepened China-Botswana cooperation can offer lessons for African nations to advance economic transition and independent development. It also serves as a model for reorienting China-Africa cooperation toward industrial upgrading. "China-Botswana cooperation shows that despite differences in economic scale, industrial structure and development stage, countries can carry out practical cooperation on the basis of equal consultation and mutual respect," Song said. "It also demonstrates that the Global South cooperation championed by China is open and inclusive, with a global vision and strong development potential."

item.title: Chinese woman's A$50 thrift-store 'blind box' yields currencies from around the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09 22:08:00
Coins from various countries are sorted after being taken out of the money jar. Photo: Xiaoxiang Morning Herald report A Chinese woman in Australia got more than she bargained for after spending A$50 ($34.70) on a secondhand money jar, only to discover dozens of currencies from around the world inside, turning the unusual thrift-store purchase into a small profit, Xiaoxiang Morning Herald reported. The woman, who goes by Stella online, told Xiaoxiang Morning Herald that she first came across the jar while casually browsing a charity thrift store on October 1, the first day of China's National Day holidays. She filmed it and posted the video online, where it quickly attracted attention. Curious viewers urged her to find out what was inside, so she returned the next day and bought it. The A$50 jar already showed a few visible banknotes and coins, including a 1-yuan Chinese banknote. Stella explained that the shop was a charity store where donated secondhand items are priced and resold, after some social media users wondered whether the seller was simply trying to make money from the mystery container. Once home, Stella spent more than two hours sorting through the haul. Among the finds were 150,000 Vietnamese dong, S$10, $5, 1 yuan and a variety of old coins. By the time she had separated the currencies into dozens of types, she said, it was already dark outside. A rough calculation put the collection's value at about 421.97 yuan ($63), leaving her more than 180 yuan ahead based on exchange rates. But Stella said she has no plans to cash in. Many of the coins are old and no longer in circulation, and she believes the original owner must have put considerable effort into collecting them. She plans to keep the collection as a souvenir. Global Times

item.title: From Northern Myanmar to the world, an anti-fraud dragnet is tightening
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09 21:52:00
A sceenshot of The Demise of Telecom Fraud in Northern Myanmar. Source: CCTV Following its broadcast, the three-part documentary The Demise of Telecom Fraud in Northern Myanmar has caught widespread attention both in China and abroad. This reaction reflects a universal aversion to telecom fraud across the international community and a shared expectation for joint decisive action. Telecom fraud is a global scourge. According to a report by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, economic losses incurred by fraud in East and Southeast Asia, Australia, and other regions reached a staggering $88.3 billion to $114.1 billion in 2025 alone - a figure that even exceeds the GDP of several countries. Perpetrators of telecom fraud have long dug in abroad, directing operations remotely. Meanwhile, funds move in seconds, digital trails are obfuscated through layers of disguise, and victims span multiple nations. Authorities shut down one fraud compound today only to see a new one spring up on another hill tomorrow, or arrest a few ringleaders here while a fresh batch of "agents" emerges elsewhere. This proves a stark reality: without cross-border cooperation - encompassing intelligence sharing, joint arrests, judicial collaboration, and repatriation - anti-fraud efforts are reduced to an endless game of "whack-a-mole," where stamping out one fire only sparks another elsewhere. How to join forces to sever the tentacles of telecom fraud has become a question that is imperative for the international community to answer. The solution demonstrated by China in this battle is to advance international cooperation through concrete action. As revealed in the third episode of the documentary Weaving the Sky Net, Chinese and Myanmar police, leveraging long-standing law enforcement and security cooperation mechanisms, carried out their first joint enforcement operation in Muse town in Myanmar, apprehending 807 telecom fraud suspects in a single sweep and eradicating the final, most stubborn "nail" that had long resisted the special crackdown. Meanwhile, the ministerial-level coordination mechanism established by China, Myanmar, and Thailand in early 2025 launched joint purges against gambling and fraud syndicates in Myanmar's Myawaddy town, carrying out 10 consecutive joint repatriation operations that led to the total demolition of more than 630 buildings in the infamous KK Park. For China, tightening this anti-fraud dragnet is both an essential requirement for safeguarding the property security of its own people and a concrete practice of fulfilling its responsibilities as a major country to build a community with a shared future for humanity. At the law enforcement level, China has repeatedly launched joint crackdown operations with Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, and other countries. At the institutional level, China and its neighboring countries have successively established trilateral coordination mechanisms among China, Myanmar, and Thailand, as well as the Lancang-Mekong law enforcement and security cooperation mechanism. Furthermore, China has helped neighboring nations build law enforcement capacity through material assistance and technical support. Not long ago, the International Alliance Combating Telecom and Cyber Fraud was established in Lianyungang, East China's Jiangsu Province, where representatives from 46 founding countries, 34 observer countries, the United Nations, Interpol, and other bodies issued a joint declaration. This marks a pivotal shift in global anti-fraud efforts - coordinated and advanced by China - from a fragmented "sweeping snow from one's own doorstep" approach to "jointly weaving an integrated global network." Combating telecom fraud is no overnight task, and in the fight against fraud, there are no bystanders. Facing telecom fraud that constantly shifts and mutates, only through broader consensus, more pragmatic measures, and a tighter network can the chain of evil be broken and the peace and well-being of millions of households safeguarded.

item.title: GT on the spot: How do Yangshan Port immigration officers pair AI screening with sniffer dogs to keep the world's busiest gateway moving?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09 21:42:00
A section of Shanghai Yangshan Deep Water Port Photo: VCG An overseas cargo vessel slowly approached the port. In the bridge, the captain could not yet make out the coastline with the naked eye, but on a giant screen at the Command Center of the Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station, about 35 nautical miles away, the ship's bright signal had already been firmly detected. The vessel berthed. The gangway was lowered. Crew members disembarked one by one, while their luggage passed through X-ray scanners, their faces were matched, and their travel documents were verified - all in a matter of seconds. At the same time, live footage was fed back to the command center in real time. On both sides of the quay crane, smart sensors automatically captured the body language, clothing and facial features of embarking and disembarking crew, with the data instantly cross-referenced against Border Inspection Clearance Channel and port security gates. This is Shanghai Yangshan Deep Water Port, the world's largest man-made deep-water port built on an island. As a key component of Shanghai Port - which has ranked first in the world in container throughput for 16 consecutive years - Yangshan Deep Water Port handled more than 28 million TEUs (twenty-foot equivalent units) in 2025, accounting for as much as 52 percent of Shanghai Port's total throughput. At this world-class hub that operates around the clock, how can security and efficiency be achieved at the same time? The Global Times reporter recently visited the Phase IV automated terminal of the Yangshan Deep Water Port, and the Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station, to experience firsthand a smart security line woven by "AI algorithms" and the "nose of police dogs." The Command Center of the Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station Photo: Huang Lanlan/GT 'All-seeing eyes' Yangshan Deep Water Port is bigger than many people imagine. More than 20,000 container trucks enter and leave the port area every day, and an average of about 450 authorized boarding personnel conduct work operations daily. Like a set of precision gears spinning at high speed, the terminal has become a vast, tightly coordinated system - one that the local immigration authorities say can no longer be effectively managed by the old-style inspection model that relied on face-to-face, on-site checks. The transformation began with an intelligent sensing system. At the Command Center of the Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station, immigration officer Li Daming demonstrated how the system works. Far out at sea, in the anchorage area, a photoelectric radar covers a radius of 30 nautical miles, bringing every vessel that enters the zone under surveillance. Closer in, detection checkpoints have been set up along the main shipping channel, through which all inbound vessels must pass. "This system has been upgraded over the past few years. It's like installing a pair of 'all-seeing eyes' on the sea," Li told the Global Times. But technology is not always enough. Some deep-sea cargo vessels have complex structures, with tightly packed containers and numerous hidden gaps and interlayers - blind spots that may escape both machines and human eyes. That is why local immigration officers also use another "tool." On an early fall afternoon at local immigration inspection station, the Global Times reporter saw suitcases being lined up on the ground. Hidden inside one of them was a small packet of cannabis. A police dog named "Manman," led by handler Zhang Xiaobin, sniffed its way slowly past the luggage, tail gently swaying. It eventually stopped beside the suitcase concealing the drugs and barked. Four-and-a-half-year-old Manman is a Labrador trained to detect narcotics and has already taken part in multiple real-world operations. In September 2023, the Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station established its police dog unit, which now has seven dogs trained for narcotics detection, explosives detection, patrol and security work, as well as special search-and-rescue tasks. In August 2025, the police dog unit helped uncover contraband during an inspection on a ship's deck. Immigration officers train police dogs to detect narcotics at Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station on August 26, 2026 Photo: Huang Lanlan/GT Better service Yangshan Deep Water Port's bustle is not confined to cargo. In the first half of 2026, more than 4,700 international vessels berthed at the port. Every day, crew members from around the world enter China through this gateway. "The route network here spans more than 200 countries and regions, and the crew come from places such as Russia, the Philippines, India, Ukraine, Sweden and Germany," said immigration officer Wang Jing. To cope with the port's high-density, high-volume operations, Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station has further streamlined clearance procedures to better serve those involved. For those who board ships to visit relatives working as crew members, the process has also become far simpler. "In the past, they had to come to the immigration inspection station in person to apply for a permit. Now, they can do it online," Wang said. Similarly, overseas crew members who need to go ashore only have to obtain a temporary entry permit for seafarers. They can submit their applications online in advance, and on-site immigration officers only need to verify their identity documents against the person present. "As long as it's within the permitted time frame, crew members can easily go shopping or sightseeing in downtown Shanghai," Wang told the Global Times. Data showed that in 2025, Yangshan Immigration Inspection Station processed 10,500 outbound vessel clearances, 259,000 passenger movements and 15,000 crew changeovers. From AI-powered "all-seeing eyes" and drug-sniffing police dogs, to almost contactless clearance, the safety and efficiency of Yangshan Deep Water Port continue to rise. "Every container at this world's largest port is tied to the national port security," Li told the Global Times. "There is no end to port development, and neither will our safeguarding efforts ever stop."

item.title: How China achieved its photovoltaic turnaround
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09 21:21:00
Solar rooftop photovoltaic power generation facilities are seen on a building in Qingdao, East China's Shandong Province, on June 23, 2026. Photo: VCG By the end of July, China's installed capacity of solar panels reached 1.286 billion kilowatts in China, surpassing that of coal power for the first time to become the nation's largest power source by installed capacity. In China, photovoltaic (PV) power has shifted from a "satellite-exclusive luxury" to a power source cheaper than coal. This remarkable turnaround offers deep insights into industrial growth and the fundamental laws of energy transition. The essence of this turnaround lies in locking the market and the factories into a single closed-loop system, driving that ecosystem toward systematic synergy and high-efficiency operation. To get this virtuous cycle spinning, the first step was a vigorous push to expand the domestic market. China has been leveraging policy coordination to anchor and open up the domestic market. Measures included shifting subsidies entirely to actual power generation output with 20-year guaranteed terms. This not only plugged loopholes prone to subsidy fraud but also provided stable, long-term revenue streams, turning solar farms into bankable assets that financial institutions were willing to lend to. The foresight of this policy lay not merely in daring to invest when solar costs remained high, but in building a mechanism that forced costs downward rather than simply throwing subsidies at enterprises to keep them afloat. Truly effective industrial policy does not replace the market; rather, it allows market forces to play out fully over long cycles. Once the market opened, cost reduction shifted to continuous technological innovation, driven by compounding, chain-reaction improvements rather than single breakthroughs. Innovations like diamond wire saws slashed silicon wafer costs and established mono-crystalline wafers as the mainstream choice, a trajectory mirrored by PERC solar cell technology. These technologies were not originally invented in China, but why were their industrialization fates ultimately rewritten in Chinese workshops? The reason lies in China's comprehensive, all-inclusive industrial supply chains and intense market competition. The moment a new manufacturing process is successfully verified and run at a single company, domestic equipment suppliers immediately step up with iterative upgrades, and industry peers race to expand production capacity, achieving widespread adoption across the entire sector within a few years. Today, China's PV industry R&D strength has entered the global vanguard. Besides, technology dictates the content of learning, while scale determines its speed. China accounts for over 80 percent of manufacturing output across all segments of the solar supply chain, meaning the vast majority of global PV industrial experience has been accumulated in China. The true weight of China's scaled industrial capacity lies in the fact that its expanding output can, by and large, find genuine, real-world demand to absorb it, be it at home or abroad. When supply can be manufactured and demand can absorb it, costs can slide steadily down the "learning curve." Of course, the industry faces pressing real-world challenges in integration and absorption. On the power grid side, midday surges in solar generation coupled with insufficient support during evening peak hours mean that energy storage deployment and market mechanisms urgently need strengthening. On the industrial side, harmonizing industrial policy with effective measures to curb cutthroat price competition and realigning the supply side with genuine market demand are vital tasks for the period ahead. From a "luxury item on satellites" to a ubiquitous fixture on deserts, rooftops, and fish ponds, solar power has journeyed for over seven decades since the invention of the silicon solar cell. The answer behind China's solar turnaround is hardly a secret: policy guided the market back home, an integrated supply chain system translated innovation into scaled manufacturing capacity, and an ultra-large market and application ecosystem further refined that capacity into seasoned industrial expertise. Chinese enterprises had paid the "tuition fee," and today, the dividends and hard-earned lessons of cost reduction are shared with the world. For the world, the profound significance of China's PV turnaround lies in shattering conventional mindsets: energy security does not have to be entirely tethered to underground reserves and maritime trade routes; at least a portion of it can be forged right inside a workshop. The author is a research fellow at the Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Risk Perception and Sustainable Governance in Energy Transition. Fu Hongdi also contributed to this article. opinion@globaltimes.com.cn
